messages:
alex: Heads-up — after last kernel roll we see a 15–25% p99 latency bump for long-prefill traffic. Looks correlated with batches that are >75% prefill tokens. KV cache churn goes up and decode kernels get slower. Profiling attached inline.

mia: Oof. Seen similar on staging earlier but at smaller magnitude. Any sign it's a single kernel regression or just batch composition?

alex: From perf dump: heavy stall in memory copies around kernel handoff. Flame fragment: 
```
[timeline] prefill_enqueue -> kv_primer -> kernel_select -> memcopy_wait -> decode_kernel
counts: prefill=120k, decode=40k, kv_hits drops ~18% during spike
````
Hash of failing batch types: mostly chat-like requests with long prompts + short generations.

jordan: Could be KV eviction/rewarm thrash when prefill dominates batch. Prefill fills KV cache with prefixes that later decode doesn't reuse. If batching groups prefill-heavy and decode-heavy together, we pay both memcopy + cold KV.

tara: Agree. Two quick levers: 1) enforce phase-aware batching (separate prefill-only batches from decode-only batches), 2) lower token_budget target for prefill-stage to avoid very large prefill batches that displace hot KV entries.

alex: Ran a quick A/B on a single node: phase-separated queue reduced p99 by ~11% and KV miss-rate improved from 22% -> 8% for the sample workload. But tail CPU increased slightly due to more smaller decode batches.

mia: Can we try a hybrid: prefer small prefill batches (token_budget cap ~512) but allow decode batches to coalesce more aggressively. Also try keeping a small sticky-KV region for recent prefixes to avoid full eviction.

jordan: Implementation notes: token_budget is global per-queue. We can introduce per-phase token_budget and a 'kv-reserve' flag on batch descriptors. Batch formation heuristics: examine incoming request metadata: if is_prefill==true, route to prefill-queue with budget X and kernel_affinity prefill-kernel; else route to decode-queue. Queue scheduler needs soft handover so decode doesn't starve when prefill backfills.

alex: Prototype patch: 
```go
// in scheduler
if req.is_prefill {
  queue := qPool.Get("prefill")
  req.tokenBudget = min(req.tokens, cfg.prefill_budget)
  queue.Push(req)
} else {
  queue := qPool.Get("decode")
  req.tokenBudget = min(req.tokens, cfg.decode_budget)
  queue.Push(req)
}
```

tara: Nice. For rollout: start with canary on low-traffic region, monitor kv_hit_rate, p50/p95/p99, and kernel_selection_count. Add automatic fallback to unified queue if p99 regresses >5% for 10m.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: patch/eng-runtime/phase-batched-prefill-decode -- canary -> us-west-2 small fleet (6 GPUs).

alex: Will watch the canary tonight and collect nvprof profiles + allocator traces. If stable, follow-up item: add 'kv-reserve' metadata so batches can mark hot prefixes to skip eviction.

mia: Also log batch composition (prefill_ratio, avg_tokens, kernel_choice) to console dashboards so product teams can see changes.

jordan: Filing short follow-ups: create perf test that synthesizes long-prefill + short-decode mix and run across kernel variants to validate kernel selection heuristics.

tara: Thanks — good plan. Keep notes in the RFC draft and ping me if canary shows any 10% regressions. :eyes:
